Choose which apps should see the VPN and which apps should not.

Selected apps CANNOT SEE THE VPN.
Enabled protection layers are applied to the selected apps and hide the VPN from them. Other eligible apps work without this protection.

Selected apps CAN SEE THE VPN.
Enabled layers become permissions for those apps. Other eligible third-party apps CANNOT SEE THE VPN.

N = kernel protection, F = Android/LSPosed protection, P = port hiding.
In Hide mode, an enabled chip hides that part of the VPN from the selected app.
In Show mode, an enabled chip lets the selected app see that part of the VPN. A check mark means the permission is enabled.

Port rules follow the same logic.
In Hide mode, the listed ports are hidden from selected apps.
In Show mode, selected apps can see the listed ports, while other eligible apps cannot.
System and privileged apps are not affected.
Safe for banks, госуслуги, marketplaces, non-browser apps. Chromium-based browsers use localhost for dev/PWA features — avoid adding them as observers.

Intercepts general interface IOCTLs (e.g., SIOCGIFFLAGS, SIOCGIFMTU) to hide VPN interface states.
Intercepts socket-level IOCTLs like SIOCGIFCONF to filter out VPN interfaces during network enumeration.
Filters VPN network interfaces out of netlink link-dump (RTM_GETLINK) responses.
Filters VPN IPv6 addresses out of netlink address-dump (RTM_GETADDR) responses.
Filters VPN IPv4 addresses out of netlink address-dump (RTM_GETADDR) responses.
Filters out VPN routes when apps read the IPv4 routing table in /proc/net/route.
Filters out VPN routes when apps read the IPv6 routing table in /proc/net/ipv6_route.
Filters out IPv4 VPN routes during netlink routing table dumps.
Filters out VPN policy routing rules from netlink rule-dump (RTM_GETRULE) responses.
Filters out IPv6 VPN routes from netlink route-dump (RTM_GETROUTE) responses.
Filters out IPv4 VPN routes from netlink route-dump (RTM_GETROUTE) responses.
Intercepts setsockopt calls to deny VPN socket binding (SO_BINDTODEVICE/IFINDEX), override SO_MARK to 0, and spoof MTU discovery.
Intercepts getsockopt calls to spoof MTU, MSS (TCP_MAXSEG), MTU discovery, and hide socket binding to a VPN interface.
Implements Port Hiding by blocking loopback connections to VPN daemon control ports.
Spoofs getsockname for IPv4 sockets, masking the local VPN interface IP with the cover interface IP.
Spoofs getsockname for IPv6 sockets, masking the local VPN interface IP with the cover interface IP.
Intercepts bind() on loopback: redirects protected ports to random free ephemeral ports (0) to bypass conflict checks.
Intercepts BPF map lookups via sys_bpf syscall to return zero traffic counters on stats maps (iface_stats, tether_stats, stats_map_) for VPN interfaces and target UIDs.

Denies access to, hides, and filters out VPN-related paths and interface listings in /sys/class/net, /proc/net/dev, /proc/net/if_inet6, /proc/net, and /proc/sys/net (returns ENOENT or removes from directory listings).
Emulates physical network queue limits (EAGAIN) and timing delays on non-blocking UDP sockets to hide virtual TUN speeds.
Blocks link-local IPv6 bind() calls on hidden VPN interface scopes to suppress NDP brute-force interface discovery.
Blocks link-local IPv6 sendto() packets directed at hidden VPN interface scopes to prevent NDP brute-force routing checks.
Filters out VPN interface references from /proc/net/fib_trie (FIB trie) output.
Filters out qdisc (traffic control) entries for VPN interfaces from RTM_GETQDISC netlink responses.

Hides the VPN interface from network enumeration APIs — getifaddrs(), ioctl, netlink, and kernel routing tables. VPN-assigned ports are intercepted at bind() and connect() to prevent port-based fingerprinting.

All Java-layer checks pass. Most native checks pass.

Not covered: socket-option probes (MTU/MSS, TCP_INFO, SO_BINDTODEVICE), GSO/PMTU side-channels, eBPF traffic-stat maps, and filesystem paths such as /sys/class/net.

Everything in Min, plus setsockopt/getsockopt interception. MTU, MSS, TCP_INFO, SO_BINDTODEVICE, and SO_TIMESTAMPING values are spoofed to match a physical interface. SO_MARK leaks are blocked. GSO and PMTU probes are neutralised. getsockname/getpeername return physical-interface addresses.

All Java and virtually all native direct-API checks pass.

Not covered: eBPF traffic statistics, filesystem enumeration (/sys/class/net, /proc/net/dev), and UDP timing side-channels.

Everything in Avg, plus:

• /proc/net/dev, /proc/net/if_inet6, /proc/net/fib_trie — VPN interface hidden from proc entries
• /sys/class/net/* — VPN interface hidden from the filesystem
• eBPF maps — VPN traffic statistics zeroed
• UDP rate-limit timing — side-channel neutralised
• IPv6 link-local bruteforce — blocked
• Traffic shaping (qdisc) — VPN qdisc hidden

Covers all known direct and indirect detection vectors.
No active VPN detected. Connect to a VPN to run diagnostic checks.
Monolithic kernel integration for maximum stealth and stability
The hiding logic is compiled directly into the kernel source as a monolithic feature. Completely eliminates modular routing latency and execution delays.
Invulnerable to timing attacks on system calls (syscalls). Because it operates natively inside the kernel code rather than as a loaded module (LKM/KPM), it leaves no footprint.
Being compiled as one monolithic unit with the kernel, it is permanent and untouchable. Eliminates runtime synchronization errors or hook decoupling.

Note: Switching is completely optional. The standard external kernel module (LKM) will continue to receive updates and function normally. You can switch to the built-in kernel version at your convenience.
